summary:
The SC-130 fix is correct. In Get-Missing (tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:470-498) a guard-stopped arm is now judged after the guardAtStart branch and before the interrupted branch. The interrupt suffix comes from whichever marks exist, and the four-field checks still run. The interrupted-without-guard branch (:500-505) is byte-identical to 0feac0e. Get-Net is an Ordinal OrderedDictionary, and every reader (:487, Format-Net :563-564) spells the keys exactly.

What I ran:
- The repro: exit 0 under pwsh and under powershell.exe 5.1, 7 ok each.
- PoolWatchCases P-003 (35 ok, both shells), P-004 (11 ok, both shells), C-053, C-054, C-055, C-056, C-027, P-001, P-002 and C-011: all exit 0.
- SL-099-ReportTextUnchanged: 21 ok in 29.5 s against a git-archive of 0feac0e.
- SL-099-TagCompareRuleCorpus 59 ok, SL-099-RecordAndEvidence 28 ok, SL-099-CasesUnderEngineTemp 16 ok.
- rules-parity: AGREE 18/22/48, 68 settled. RuleCases C-001 and C-003: exit 0.
- Fitness check: 90 rules hold.
- harness.py --only S44-S50: 7 AS-RECORDED, and it left no scratch.
- The spike-107 evidence matches its three source run folders byte for byte. Only output.txt and the 0-byte files were left out, as declared.

Each case-matrix test feeds its shape in. For example, X1 in the repro and in P-003 fixture 2 really has guardStop, exitCode -1, interrupted true, killed false and no /settled. P-004's marks really list Ntff before NtfF.

Two minor defects, both new members of the 'case-folding tag comparison spellings' family that O-018 says is closed:
- The first fitness entry has no (?i). PowerShell operator names ignore case, so `$WatchedTags -Contains $_[0]` passes both entries.
- Compare-Object and Select-String fold case like Group-Object does, and no pattern covers them.

For both, I measured that the proposed fix keeps 0 hits on PoolWatch.ps1 and keeps every quiet corpus row quiet. Nothing in the tree breaks either rule today.

Second round: Second round, read as someone trying to break it. Two things were checked and hold:
- Get-Missing's guard branch holds for the arm-line and mark shapes a real run can write.
- Get-ScratchParent is not fooled by a forward-slash TEMP: GetTempPath normalises it to C:\Windows\Temp\, measured.

One new member of the case-folding family round 1 already filed. Both fitness entries assume the tag is reached as `$_.tag`, a bare word `tag`, or `$_[0]`. A quoted or indexed property name gets past every one of the ten patterns:
- `$_['tag'] -eq $name`
- `$_.'tag' -eq $name`
- `Where-Object -Property 'tag' -EQ`
- `switch ($row['tag'])`
- `$name -eq $_['tag']`

Measured: each of these gets 0 hits, and `$_['tag'] -eq 'NtfF'` over live `[ordered]` tag entries returns Ntff's entry. PoolWatch.ps1 uses `$x['key']` indexing 16 times, and Read-Mark builds every live tag entry as `[ordered]@{ tag = ... }` (:213), so this spelling is house style, not a contrivance. A candidate pattern pair catches all six spellings, gives 0 hits on PoolWatch.ps1, and leaves every quiet corpus row quiet, all measured.

Looked at and not filed:
- Group-Object -CaseSensitive -AsHashTable under 5.1 gives a loud key-duplication error, not a silent merge.
- The corpus test's comment blanking is stricter than needed, and Fitness itself is the gate.
- P-004 finds the NtfF column by its position from the end (`$cells[-4]`), so adding a tag to $NetTags will turn it red, not falsely green.

findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1176-1178 (entry 'PoolWatch never compares pool tag names without regard to case'); tests/window/PoolWatchTagCompareCorpus.json rows T10, T11, T13, T18; measured with the patterns read from fitness.yaml as SL-099-TagCompareRuleCorpus.Tests.ps1 reads them.
findings.fix:
Prefix the three patterns at .taad/fitness.yaml:1176-1178 with (?i). Measured: still 0 hits on the blanked PoolWatch.ps1 and no hit on any quiet corpus row, because `-ccontains`, `-cin` and `-ceq` still cannot match `-i?(contains|in|eq)`.

Add these corpus rows:
- fire: `$all | Where-Object { $WatchedTags -Contains $_[0] }`
- fire: `if ($name -In $WatchedTags) { $x = 1 }`
- fire: `if ($t -EQ 'NtfF') { $x = 1 }`
- quiet: `$all | Where-Object { $WatchedTags -CContains $_[0] }`

Optionally add a plant row beside S50 with the capitalised operator.

findings.claim:
Compare-Object and Select-String fold case by default, the same way Group-Object and Sort/Select-Object -Unique do. The build added Group-Object and -Unique to this family as a declared deviation, then stopped. Measured: `Compare-Object @('NtfF') @('Ntff')` reports 0 differences, and 2 with -CaseSensitive.

No pattern in either entry sees these cmdlets:
- `$new = Compare-Object $before.tags.tag $after.tags.tag -PassThru` gets 0 hits;
- `$hit = @($mark.tags.tag | Select-String -Pattern 'NtfF' -SimpleMatch)` gets 0 hits.

Compare-Object is the natural way to ask which tags appeared between two marks, and it would treat NtfF and Ntff as one tag. The outcome-C reading rule decides on exactly those two.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1189-1196 (entry 'PoolWatch compares pool tags case-exactly', whose Group-Object and -Unique patterns are at :1195-1196); tests/window/PoolWatchTagCompareCorpus.json has no Compare-Object or Select-String row.
findings.fix:
Add this pattern to 'PoolWatch compares pool tags case-exactly':
`(?i)\b(?:Compare-Object|Select-String)\b(?![^\r\n]*-CaseSensitive)[^\r\n]*\btag\b`
Measured: 0 hits on PoolWatch.ps1 and no quiet corpus row hit.

Add these corpus rows:
- fire: `$new = Compare-Object $before.tags.tag $after.tags.tag -PassThru`
- fire: `$hit = @($mark.tags.tag | Select-String -Pattern 'NtfF' -SimpleMatch)`
- quiet: `Compare-Object -CaseSensitive $before.tags.tag $after.tags.tag`

findings.claim:
Both fitness entries assume the tag is reached as `.tag`, a bare word `tag`, or `$_[0]`. A quoted or indexed property name, legal PowerShell for the same lookup, gets past every one of the ten patterns.

Measured 0 hits for each of:
- `@($mark.tags | Where-Object { $_['tag'] -eq $name })[0]`
- `$_["tag"] -ieq $name`
- `$_.'tag' -eq $name`
- `Where-Object -Property 'tag' -EQ -Value $name`
- `switch ($row['tag']) { 'NtfF' { ... } }`
- `if ($name -eq $_['tag'])`

All of them fold case. Over live entries listing Ntff before NtfF, `$_['tag'] -eq 'NtfF'` returned Ntff's entry (pa 900, not 7).

This spelling is the file's own idiom:
- PoolWatch.ps1 indexes its ordered dictionaries with `$x['key']` 16 times (Invoke-ExeArm's `$line['guardStop']` and others);
- Read-Mark builds each live tag entry as `[ordered]@{ tag = $_[0]; ... }` (:213), where `$_['tag']` works.
A live-mark tag lookup written in that style, for example by the measurement-preparation slice's guard-trip or cancel-trigger work, would pass both rules.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1190 (pattern 1 needs the word `tag` directly before whitespace and an operator), :1191 and :1193 (the right-hand side and switch forms need `\$[\w.]*tag\b`); tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:213 builds tag entries as [ordered]@{ tag = ... }; tests/window/PoolWatchTagCompareCorpus.json has no quoted or indexed row.
findings.fix:
Add two patterns to 'PoolWatch compares pool tags case-exactly':
- `(?i)(?:\[\s*['"]tag['"]\s*\]|\.['"]tag['"]|-Property\s+['"]tag['"])\s*-i?(eq|ne|like|notlike|match|notmatch|in|notin|contains|notcontains)\b(?!\s*\$null\b)`
- `(?i)(?:\bswitch\s*\(\s*\$[\w.]*|-i?(?:eq|ne|like|notlike|match|notmatch|contains|notcontains|in|notin)\s+\$[\w.]*)(?:\[\s*['"]tag['"]\s*\]|\.['"]tag['"])`
Measured: all six lines above fire, 0 hits on the blanked PoolWatch.ps1, and no quiet corpus row hit.

Add the six lines to the corpus as fire rows. Add these as quiet rows:
- `@($mark.tags | Where-Object { $_['tag'] -ceq $name })[0]`
- `if ($_['tag'] -eq $null) { continue }`
- `switch -CaseSensitive ($row['tag']) { 'NtfF' { 1 } }`
- `$line['guardStop'] = $x`

drift: The build lists 'committing the repro' as not built. That is out of date: commit d2620fc ('SL-099 build attempt 1') includes tests/bugs/SL-099-GuardStopSurvivesInterrupt.Tests.ps1, so the design's 'SC-130 acceptance test, committed' component is in the tree.

The build claims 'P-003/P-004/C-056 also pass under powershell.exe'. PoolWatchCases' Invoke-Report always launches `pwsh` for -Report, so under powershell.exe those cases do not run Get-Missing or Format-Net in 5.1. Only the repro, which launches -Report with its own host, does, along with P-004's in-process Get-Net call. O-003 rests on the repro.

O-044 (F1 is cold) and O-045 (F1's cache survives to F2-F5) are owed to validate-slice. Both can only be measured in the person's session 1: a true Restart and whole-C: F1-F5 scans, which the engine may not run unattended (lesson #357, CC-006). Unless they are retargeted to a person, validate will hold on them.

Get-ScratchParent now exists as three copies: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1, the repro and tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1. The design asked for the copy, but a later fix to one will not reach the others.

Invoke-Report still calls Check, which uses Write-Output, inside a function whose return value is used. The 'no line carries a judgement word' ok line becomes part of $r and is never printed; a FAIL is still counted in $script:Failures. This was already so at 0feac0e. The build moved the two echo lines to Write-Host for this same reason but left this one.
